clue.text: Get down! Get down here

definitions.meaning: a shouted order to drop low and avoid something thrown
the soft feathers called down come from this water bird, as in eiderdown

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to bob quickly out of harm's way, and the noun names the bird whose breast feathers give us down.

clue.text: Ordered book on CIA dirty tricks

indicators.note: dirty tricks plays on the letters, which are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A book exposing the CIA's dirty tricks has been commissioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like 'commissioned' but describes a book arranged in alphabetical order; 'tricks' reshuffles ON CIA DIRTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a reference book whose entries are arranged in strict alphabetical order.

clue.text: Tea died in arable land, one bordering Euphrates once

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: the letter for died goes inside the word for the field

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field
d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone's tea plantation perished on farmland near an ancient river.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient region of southern Mesopotamia lay along the lower Euphrates, so it bordered the river in antiquity.

clue.text: Improper behaviour of two nose-wipers, only one taking correct head

annotationWithheld.why: Improper behaviour of two nose-wipers, only one taking correct head (5-5): HANKY twice with the second's H made P, but no sound reading of 'correct' gives P; parse unconfirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Improper behaviour of two nose-wipers, only one taking correct head

clue.text: Nelson perhaps holding British over European as deserving of respect

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over, above, the next
the naval officer holds the letter for British inside him

parts.note: Horatio Nelson was a famous British admiral

explanation.surface: Lord Nelson's grip on British interests over Europe earns praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worthy of admiration is deserving of respect; the two phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Writer portraying a fine king in the spirit of Rameses

indicators.note: the short run of letters is placed in the word for the spirit

parts.note: in Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spiritual double, so a pharaoh such as Rameses had one
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An author depicts a fine pharaoh in a story about the spirit of Rameses.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz of that surname was a Prague-born novelist, author of The Trial, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Claimant to throne has advantage during fighting over stream

indicators.note: in a down clue the first parts sit over the stream

parts.note: a perk is a benefit or advantage
in can mean during, as in 'in the night'
war is fighting
a beck is a northern English word for a brook

explanation.surface: A pretender to the crown gains the upper hand in a battle across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: BECK is a northern English dialect word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the pretender who claimed to be Richard, Duke of York, against Henry VII in the 1490s.

clue.text: Barrier rises after chap turns up with this?

definitions.text: Barrier rises after chap turns up with this?

indicators.note: the reversed barrier is placed after the reversed chap
in a down clue the word for chap reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for barrier reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: A gate is lifted when a man arrives wearing the right identification.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'turns up' and 'rises' are reversal signals in a down entry; the whole clue also describes a badge that gets a visitor through a raised barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge bearing your name can get you waved through a security barrier when you turn up.

clue.text: Turning up no good philosophical principle

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for no is turned so it reads upwards

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A rule of philosophy rejects goodness as it rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' looks like NG, but 'no' gives NAY, turned to YAN, and 'good' adds G.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chinese thought this is the active, masculine principle paired with yin.

clue.text: Head copper guarding princess's millions

indicators.note: the symbol for copper surrounds the princess as a guard would

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rani is an Indian queen or princess

explanation.surface: A senior policeman protects a royal's fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head copper' reads as a chief constable, but 'Head' is the definition and 'copper' the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony case enclosing the brain is the skull, the upper part of the head.

clue.text: Not often seen dressed for rugby in Oxford, having to work steadily

parts.note: rugby players wear shorts, so someone dressed for the game is in them
up means in residence at a university such as Oxford
to ply is to work at something steadily

explanation.surface: A student at Oxford is rarely seen in rugby kit because of steady study.
explanation.walkthrough: UP is the British usage for being in residence at a university, so a student is 'up at Oxford'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce and seldom available is rarely encountered, hence not often seen.

clue.text: Decree about energy he puts out at work

indicators.note: the word for decree goes about the letter for energy

parts.note: a firman is an edict issued by an oriental ruler
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An edict concerning energy is issued by someone at his job.
explanation.definitionFit: A firefighter's job is extinguishing blazes, putting fires out as his daily work.

clue.text: Ford, perhaps, in river Test is leading to centre of Upton

parts.note: the Indus is a great river of Pakistan
a trial is a test

indicators.note: only the middle letter of the town name is taken

explanation.surface: A river crossing on the Test leads into the middle of an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like a river crossing on the Test, a Hampshire river, but it is Henry Ford the carmaker, and 'Test' gives TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Ford built a huge car-making business, an example of a manufacturing magnate.

clue.text: Just their thing? Wrong!

indicators.note: the exclamation says the two words are set out wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that it is not quite their sort of thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like an adverb meaning 'merely'; it is the definition, meaning fair or correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To be just is to be fair and justified, the same as being correct in a dispute.

clue.text: Beginnings of new growth around infected oak tree

indicators.note: the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Fresh shoots have sprouted around an oak that has caught a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a New Zealand tree, also known from the crime writer Ngaio Marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small evergreen tree native to New Zealand.

clue.text: Black and green with pale border is something fashionable all of a sudden

definitions.text: something fashionable all of a sudden

parts.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

indicators.note: the word for pale forms a border round the word for green

parts.note: wan means pale
go is the green traffic light

explanation.surface: A dark and green design edged with a pale trim has suddenly come into style.
explanation.walkthrough: GO stands for green because a green light means go.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement or cause that suddenly attracts many followers is one everybody jumps on.

clue.text: Queen on the Nile — one bird on often flooded area, to put it another way

indicators.note: the whole run is put the other way round, read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a tit is a small bird
re means on or concerning
a fen is low marshy land often under water

explanation.surface: An Egyptian queen sees a bird on a marsh beside the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put it another way' reverses ITITREFEN entirely; 'on' gives RE, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: She was a celebrated Egyptian queen, wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten.

clue.text: What needs baste for English cooking

definitions.text: What needs baste for English cooking

indicators.note: cooking the letters stirs them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A recipe note says a joint must be basted for English cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' looks like part of the kitchen picture but shuffles BASTE, FOR and E; the whole clue also describes the joint itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint roasting in the oven is spooned over with its own juices, and England's national dish is the classic example.

clue.text: All but outer parts of Cornish flower used several times as fodder plant

indicators.note: everything except the outermost letters of the run is kept
the river name is repeated, here three times over

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, and the Fal is a river in Cornwall
the third copy of the Cornish river

explanation.surface: Most of a Cornish bloom is fed repeatedly to livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river, the thing that flows; FALFALFAL loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is a leguminous crop grown widely to feed cattle and horses.

clue.text: Head of BBC before it had shows?

indicators.note: the words show, put on display, the letters within them

explanation.surface: Someone asks who ran the BBC before it had any programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: John Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC, in charge when it began broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Reith was the first Director-General and so the first chief of the British Broadcasting Corporation.

clue.text: Present from the beginning, I note remorse setting in a bit late

annotationWithheld.why: Present from the beginning, I note remorse setting in a bit late (7): I + N + B + UILT seems built from GUILT, but no parse uses 'setting in' and 'late' without a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Present from the beginning, I note remorse setting in a bit late

clue.text: One starting organisation as a result of unruly mob referendum

indicators.note: an unruly crowd is disorderly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A society is set up after a rowdy crowd's vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who belonged to a club or society from its foundation is one of its original members.

clue.text: Depressingly dull daughter's back

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for daughter
the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A girl's spine is in a sorry state.
explanation.definitionFit: This poetic word means gloomy and dismal, the same as dreary.

clue.text: Small creature runs in confusion

indicators.note: the letter for runs goes in the word for confusion

parts.note: a fog is a state of mental confusion
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A tiny animal scurries about in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: This tailless amphibian is a small animal.

clue.text: Lighter turns, having emptied space, to go back

indicators.note: turning means the word for lighter is read backwards

parts.note: paler means lighter in colour

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cigarette lighter revolves in an empty room before returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a device for lighting cigarettes but is the adjective PALER, turned to RELAP; emptied 'space' leaves SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip back into a former state, such as illness or a bad habit, is to regress.

clue.text: Suspicion Heather is going after Mark

indicators.note: the plant name follows the word for mark

parts.note: to ink is to mark with ink
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather is pursuing a man called Mark, and people suspect something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' and 'Mark' look like people's names; they are the plant LING and INK.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint or faint notion of something is a vague suspicion.

clue.text: In America, dull to teach about very easy opportunity of profit

indicators.note: the American word for dull goes about the letter for very

parts.note: gray is the American spelling of grey, meaning dull
to train is to teach

explanation.surface: In the United States, teaching is dull work but an easy way of making money.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom describes a job or scheme that yields money for very little effort.

clue.text: Ignore altered material son cut from hat

indicators.note: the word son is removed from the hat's name

parts.note: a Stetson is a broad-brimmed cowboy hat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A son disregards the changed fabric and trims his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a proofreader's mark meaning 'let it stand', telling the printer to disregard a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor writes this Latin 'let it stand' in the margin so that a marked change is disregarded.
